newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - BUBA holds rates steady, markets react calmly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BUBA holds rates steady, markets react calmly.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting, in line with the expectations of economists and financial markets.
The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at three percent.

A Reuter poll of economists this week showed that none of the 10 polled expected any change in the central bank's credit policies this week and German bond and share markets showed almost no response to the expected move.

German shares were barely moved in midday-bourse trade after the Bundesbank made its announcement. Traders said Bund weakness, Wall Street and the dollar's failure to post further gains against the mark were all holding the market down.
The 30-share DAX index was down 19.37 points at 2,683.62. IBIS DAX, which measures all-day electronic trade, down 1.77 at 2,683.46.
German bonds or Bunds and Bund futures, already trading lower, showed little movement on the Bundesbank news, with the market focusing on the U.S, market.
The 6.25 percent April 2006 Bund was trading at 101.74, up from 101.71, for a yield of 5.99 percent. The December Bund future was trading down at 99.56, compared with 99.91 at Wednesday's close.
There had been some talk in financial markets on Wednesday of a further ease in the securities repurchase rate, but most traders had dismissed the rumour, saying such a move was unlikely.

In fact, most economists have now come to the conclusion that German rates may finally have bottomed at current levels, with all of those polled this week predicting no further rate cuts in this interest rate cycle.
"Interest rates are going to remain unchanged for some time," said Holger Fahrinkrug, economist at UBS in Frankfurt.
The discount and repo rates are already at historic lows.
